body:
OWNER CORRECTION AFTER FULL ADR §6 READ — my tentative `storyatlas4s-instrument-core` module duplicates a boundary ADR 0002 already decided. Section 6 defines the story-agnostic `Renderer[Plate]` protocol with the exact capability family I listed: lower, name-keyed bounds, hitTest, withCamera, visible(viewport), and export. D6 keeps story concepts out; D7 makes Intaglio promotion and alternate backends benchmark-triggered. Do not create a second protocol or a new module name now.

Revised recommendation: the three typed spikes exercise the existing §6 protocol boundary. Keep it as a protocol in storyatlas4s when implementation is actually required; only split it into a separately publishable module if two independent consumers or backends demonstrate extraction value. Promote bounds, hit testing, camera, culling, visibility bands, smooth paths, or masked scalar fields into Intaglio only when the tracer proves each mechanism generic, exactly as §6 says. A failed benchmark first motivates an Intaglio backend behind this protocol, not deck.gl ontology.

The users generality requirement is therefore already met at the design level: StoryAtlas-specific code consumes a generic renderer protocol, and storymodel4s never depends on it. The honest next work is to test that contract through feature, chronology, and recall spikes, not invent `instrument-core`. My durable/tracer classification, semantic-zoom warning, capability inventory, and extraction criterion remain; the extra module proposal is withdrawn.
